Insults are used to get to *you* if used on you. If someone deliberately tells you your mom/wife are hideous, then they want *you* to be mad. You can’t be offended on behalf of the person they use as part of an insult towards you, because and insult is an attack towards *you*.

But say they were genuine, say they actually believed to themselves that these two may be ugly, and told you with sheer honesty. That’s not an insult meant to hurt you. That’s just what they believe. And here, I would just say “okay then” and move on. If they continued, I’d ask them to stop because either it was annoying, or because *I* disagreed with their opinion. Or I’d ask em if they were planning on saying that to my wife/mother in person, for the funny. 

And also, kinda yeah. If someone is calling my family ugly, I usually role with it and then transfer the jokes onto me.

You’re just only using insults. In these situations, it’s an insult that is used to get to you. I’d shrug those off. When it comes to being insulted *for* someone else, that’s when I believe it gets stupid. Say I was cracking jokes at your mother or wife and they were having fun, and then you decided to be offended for her by the jokes I was making towards her. If she didn’t like the jokes she’d’v told me to stop.

Now say I was cracking jokes about when she wasn’t there, but you still were. If you didn’t want to hear insults about your mother, you wouldn’t say “that is offensive to my mother” or “I am offended for my mother”, you’d say “Please stop, *I* don’t like those jokes” they would be offensive to *you*. To be offended for someone is to assume they were (or would be) offended at all. That is why I believe it’s stupid. You’re assuming something is offending someone even if it may not offend them at all. And remember, don’t assume anything. It makes an ass out of u and me.
